investigations.title: Spacecraft Fire Experiment IV
investigations.description: Saffire IV studied large-scale solid-fuel fires inside an uncrewed Cygnus spacecraft after departure from the International Space Station. Retained tables report selected sample conditions and published outcomes; they are not the raw sensor archive.
investigations.objective: Examine flame growth and spread at spacecraft-relevant scales and the resulting changes in the vehicle atmosphere to inform fire safety.
investigations.approach: Ignite solid samples in a ventilated Cygnus experiment and compare flame behavior, calorimetry, temperatures and combustion-product measurements. Keep fuel, pressure, oxygen, geometry and measurement method attached to each reported result.
investigations.hardware: Saffire apparatus in Cygnus cargo spacecraft

investigations.title: Solid Fuel Ignition and Extinction
investigations.description: SoFIE is a shared ISS research facility for solid-material ignition, flame spread, extinction and suppression. Its five investigations address different materials and mechanisms; the program is not one experimental cohort.
investigations.objective: Understand the ignition and flammability of spacecraft materials in realistic geometries and atmospheres, and improve material selection, modeling and suppression methods.
investigations.approach: Use an insert within the Combustion Integrated Rack, with shared sample holders, flow control, heaters, igniters and diagnostics. Follow the individual investigations for their conditions and results.
investigations.hardware: SoFIE insert in the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)

investigations.title: SoFIE — Residence Time Driven Flame Spread
investigations.description: Study steady and unsteady spread over solid fuel sheets in microgravity, including the relationship between fuel thickness and radiative heat loss. NASA documented actual SoFIE-RTDFS acrylic-sheet flight research in March 2025.
investigations.objective: Determine how residence time, fuel thickness and radiation affect flame propagation and quenching.
investigations.approach: Investigate acrylic-sheet flames in the SoFIE facility. The March 2025 NASA report describes elevated oxygen and half standard Earth atmospheric pressure; it is descriptive evidence, not a numerical flight-data release.
investigations.hardware: SoFIE insert in the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)

investigations.description: Study flame growth and extinction around thick PMMA spheres in microgravity, including changing internal fuel heating. Five selected extinction cases are retained from a 2024 publication.

investigations.title: Flammability Limits at Reduced-g Experiment
investigations.description: FLARE connects material flammability limits measured on Earth with behavior in microgravity. The retained NASA sources describe an international research program and early ground test-method work.
investigations.objective: Develop a method to estimate microgravity flammability limits from reproducible ground-test data.
investigations.approach: Combine ground experiments, parabolic flights and theory, with ISS/Kibo verification described in the historical NASA approach. Compare ignition methods and failure criteria before relating ground screening to low-gravity behavior.
investigations.hardware: JAXA Solid Combustion hardware described for ISS/Kibo; ground flammability apparatus
investigations.platform: Ground and reduced-gravity research; historical ISS/Kibo verification plan

investigations.title: Flammability of Materials on the Moon
investigations.description: FM2 is a lunar-surface experiment concept for measuring solid-material flame spread in one-sixth gravity. The retained 2026 requirements describe planned fabric tests and initial atmospheres; they are not lunar measurements.
investigations.objective: Observe flame spread on the Moon, evaluate whether some materials can be more flammable in partial gravity, and connect terrestrial screening with reduced-gravity behavior.
investigations.approach: Operate a sealed autonomous chamber with four separately initiated fuel samples, cameras and gas/temperature sensors. Planned initial atmospheres and exposed sample geometry are retained as condition records, separately from measured outcomes.
investigations.hardware: Sealed autonomous chamber with cameras and gas/temperature sensors

investigations.title: Lunar Combustion Investigation
investigations.description: LUCI measured solid-fuel combustion in simulated lunar gravity created by a rotating New Shepard sounding rocket. Published comparison tables report flame-spread fit rates for fabric and a PMMA rod; this was not a lunar-surface experiment.
investigations.objective: Demonstrate extended-duration material flammability research in partial gravity and compare flame behavior with related Earth-gravity experiments.
investigations.approach: Use centrifugal acceleration from a steady 11 RPM rotation and image two simultaneously burning samples with orthogonal cameras. Retain the changing oxygen concentration, Coriolis context and paired endpoints when interpreting source-reported fit rates.
investigations.hardware: Rotating combustion enclosure, orthogonal cameras and chamber oxygen measurement
investigations.platform: Blue Origin New Shepard sounding rocket
